accepted_findings.reason: Reviewed false-positive TM1 findings in the static-only PR inspection procedure: --no-checkout prevents Git from materializing attacker-controlled content or invoking checkout-time hooks and filters, while rmdir is limited to workflow-owned temporary directories after exact worktree registration and empty-directory checks; neither construct bypasses a safety gate. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-19 against content unchanged since acceptance: the mandatory --no-checkout and core.hooksPath=/dev/null guards, the exact `git worktree list --porcelain` registration match, the find-based emptiness proof before any forced removal, and the rmdir-only parent cleanup are all still present.

Re-reviewed false-positive TM1 finding: the flagged force-with-lease text is a restack instruction in the maintenance section instructing the agent NOT to force-push individual stack branches. The skill's only push paths are gh stack push/submit/sync, which push all stack branches atomically with --force-with-lease and are the documented safe mechanism for stacked branches. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27 after later edits: the flagged text still forbids plain --force-with-lease pushes of a single stack branch in favor of the atomic gh stack push.

Reviewed intentional TM1 finding for this user-triggered rebase skill: the force-push is limited to the validated current branch, uses --force-with-lease, and requires the workflow's confirmation or explicit --force-push/--auto authorization; non-auto conflict paths additionally require passing verification or a user confirmation, and every bypassed red flag or unavailable/failed verification is reported. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27 after later edits: the only model-invoked path is kramme:pr:fix-ci delegation with --force-push, which skips only the final confirmation and still stops on red flags before pushing, and the flagged push remains the validated current-branch --force-with-lease procedure.

Re-reviewed false-positive TM1 findings: every flagged --no-verify occurrence explicitly forbids bypassing hooks or gates, requires root-cause fixes, and stops for user approval before any justified disablement. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27 after later edits: the flagged --no-verify occurrence is still in the list of prohibited silent gate bypasses.

Re-reviewed intentional TM1 finding for post-consolidation publication: history rewriting requires an unshared branch or explicit collaborator coordination, and the push uses force-with-lease for ordinary branches or a restack followed by atomic gh stack push for stacked branches. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27: content unchanged since acceptance, and the CI-pinned SkillSpector scan still reports only the matches described above.

Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27: content unchanged since acceptance, and the CI-pinned SkillSpector scan still reports only the matches described above.

Re-reviewed intentional TM1 finding for this user-triggered history-recreation skill: destructive reset requires a recovery ref plus repeated branch, tip, worktree, and reset-collision validation; --auto authorizes only one unstacked branch, while automatic stack-wide rewriting requires separate --authorize-history-rewrite approval and non-auto stack-wide rewriting requires distinct interactive confirmations that enumerate the frozen stack before local restacking and atomic publication; the final tree must match the original tip; and unstacked publication freezes one URL/ref/lease, rejects mismatched or base-branch targets and push-destination-only commits, disables tag following, and uses force-with-lease.

Re-reviewed false-positive TM1 finding for the commit-readiness warning: the skill explicitly prohibits using --no-verify when hooks fail and instructs the user to fix the hook failure first. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27 after later edits: the flagged line still requires explicit user approval for --no-verify and directs fixing the hook failure first.

Re-reviewed intentional TM1 finding for Pull Request publication: the fresh path uses an empty-expectation lease only for a branch proven absent, while the existing-remote path freezes one push endpoint, revalidates branch, clean-tree, immutable source OID, strict-ancestor, and remote-tip state, then uses an exact observed-OID lease with one refspec and tag following disabled. Both modes fail closed on concurrent Git-ref updates and never replace remote-only work; Pull Request ownership sequencing remains a separate workflow policy decision. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27 after later edits: both flagged pushes still use the absence lease for the proven-absent fresh ref or the exact observed-OID lease with tag following disabled, and plain --force remains forbidden.

Re-reviewed intentional TM1 finding for the Pull Request creation rollback path: remote-append rollback validates the clean worktree, branch, and exact prepared tip immediately before using reset --keep, while fresh-mode hard reset restores only the feature branch to the full original commit after strict branch-name and full-commit-ID validation; both paths preserve the recreation backup ref for manual recovery. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27 after later edits: the flagged reset --keep still runs inside the single bounded ownership guard, and reset --hard still runs only after strict branch-name and full-commit-ID validation.

Re-reviewed intentional SC3 finding for the vendored D3 v7.9.0 minified distribution: the file still matches the pinned SHA-256 in references/sources.yaml, its complete ISC notice ships as assets/d3-LICENSE, and it is embedded locally so private Pull Request context never depends on third-party CDN execution. Re-reviewed on 2026-09-27: content unchanged since acceptance, and the CI-pinned SkillSpector scan still reports only the matches described above.

Reviewed false-positive AST4 finding: subprocess.run executes the fixed git binary with an explicit argument vector and shell=False; callers supply fixed Git subcommands, an allowlisted archive key, and paths normalized by _normalize_path, stdout and stderr are captured, and no user text reaches a shell.

Reviewed false-positive OH1 finding: the git() wrapper never builds a shell string. Every argument is a fixed subcommand, an allowlisted archive key, a validated repository path (no absolute, `..`, leading `-`, or control characters), or a commit message passed as one argv element after `-m`; nothing is interpolated into command text.

Reviewed false-positive OH1 finding: the git() wrapper runs `git` from PATH with an argument list and no shell. Caller-supplied revisions reach git only as one argv element after `rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options`; every later diff, ls-tree, and cat-file call receives the resolved commit or blob object ID and the constant policy path. No model output or diff content is passed to a command.

Reviewed false-positive PE3 findings: the `.env` / `.env.*` name check here and the credential name and suffix tables it imports from risk_patterns.py (`.npmrc`, `.netrc`, key-file suffixes) are compared against changed-path names and suffixes from `git diff --raw` to raise the path:secrets-config routing signal. The script never opens those files from disk or transmits them; their added lines are pattern-matched in memory from git diff output, the policy blob is read from the trusted `--policy-rev` (the default branch), and only paths, line numbers, and pattern names are reported.

Reviewed false-positive PE3 findings: this static table module only defines the credential file names (`.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `.pypirc`, `id_rsa`, and similar), key-file suffixes, and example-env suffixes that risk-signals.py compares against changed-path names and suffixes from `git diff --raw` to raise the path:secrets-config routing signal. Nothing here opens, reads, or transmits a file; the module contains constants and compiled patterns only.

Reviewed intentional LP3 finding: the run-state helper writes only inside the validated, git-ignored `.context/<archive-key>/reviews/` directory and commits only paths the convergence policy already classified; the skill body documents those side effects and the frontmatter schema has no permissions field.

Reviewed false-positive AST4 finding: run() passes an explicit argument vector to subprocess.run with shell=False, empty stdin, captured output, a timeout, and prompts disabled. Every argv is fixed git or gh subcommands plus values the helper validates first: the Linear branch must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]* and pass git check-ref-format --branch, the base comes from refs/remotes/origin/HEAD and passes the same check, and commit IDs must match the repository's object-ID pattern. No user text reaches a shell.
